key_insight: Bayesian inference applied to photoluminescence imaging and drift-diffusion simulations can localize whether perovskite solar cell degradation originates at the interfaces or in the bulk.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster diagnosis of stability failures and helps guide targeted passivation and fabrication strategies for more durable perovskite devices.
method: Photoluminescence imaging of fully fabricated perovskite solar cells
Drift-diffusion simulations linked to experimental observables
Bayesian inference to produce spatially resolved parameter maps during aging
evidence_signal: Under accelerated aging conditions (70 °C, full-spectrum sunlight), the inferred maps revealed strong spatial heterogeneity and identified the largest degradation in perovskite/transport-layer interfacial regions.
watch_item: The inferred degradation locations depend on model assumptions and the quality of imaging-to-simulation mapping, so calibration and validation are critical.
paper_title: Disentangling the origin of degradation in perovskite solar cells via optical imaging and Bayesian inference
